title: Python asyncio event loop basics
text: Python's asyncio module provides an event loop that schedules coroutines using async and await. Coroutines yield control at await points, letting the loop run other tasks concurrently on a single thread.

title: Rust ownership and borrowing
text: Rust's ownership system enforces memory safety without a garbage collector. Every value has a single owner, and borrowing lets code read or mutate a value temporarily through references checked at compile time.

title: Kubernetes pods and deployments
text: A Kubernetes pod is the smallest deployable unit, wrapping one or more containers. Deployments manage replica sets of pods, handling rolling updates and self-healing when pods crash.

title: Transformer attention mechanism explained
text: The transformer architecture relies on self-attention to weigh how much each token in a sequence should attend to every other token, replacing recurrence with parallelizable matrix operations.

title: Git rebase versus merge
text: Git rebase rewrites commit history onto a new base, producing a linear log, while merge preserves history with an explicit merge commit joining two branches.

title: Docker multi-stage builds
text: Multi-stage Docker builds use multiple FROM statements in one Dockerfile so a final image can copy only the compiled artifacts from earlier build stages, keeping the runtime image small.

title: React hooks and functional components
text: React hooks like useState and useEffect let functional components manage local state and side effects without writing a class component.

title: PostgreSQL indexing strategies
text: PostgreSQL supports B-tree, hash, GIN and GiST indexes. Choosing the right index type depends on the query pattern, such as equality lookups versus full-text search.

title: Unit testing with pytest fixtures
text: Pytest fixtures provide reusable setup and teardown logic for tests, injected as function parameters and composable across a test suite.

title: TF-IDF and cosine similarity for text retrieval
text: TF-IDF weights terms by how frequent they are in a document relative to how rare they are across the collection, and cosine similarity measures the angle between two such term-weight vectors.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation overview
text: RAG systems retrieve relevant documents from an external corpus and pass them as context to a language model, grounding generated answers in retrieved evidence rather than relying only on the model's parameters.

title: Vector databases and approximate nearest neighbor search
text: Vector databases like Chroma or FAISS index dense embeddings and support approximate nearest neighbor search, trading a small amount of recall for large speedups over exact search.

title: Python type hints and static checking
text: Python type hints annotate function signatures and variables with expected types, which tools like mypy can check statically without affecting runtime behavior.

title: Rust's Result type and error handling
text: Rust represents recoverable errors with the Result enum, forcing callers to explicitly handle the Ok or Err case instead of relying on exceptions.

title: Kubernetes service discovery and networking
text: Kubernetes services give a stable virtual IP and DNS name to a set of pods, so other workloads can reach them even as individual pod IPs change.

title: Fine-tuning versus prompting large language models
text: Fine-tuning updates a model's weights on task-specific data, while prompting steers a frozen model's behavior purely through the input text, trading customization depth for lower cost and faster iteration.

title: Continuous integration pipelines with GitHub Actions
text: GitHub Actions workflows run jobs triggered by repository events like pushes or pull requests, commonly used to lint, test and build a project automatically before merging.

title: Database transaction isolation levels
text: Isolation levels such as read committed, repeatable read and serializable trade consistency guarantees for concurrency, controlling what a transaction can see of other in-flight transactions.

title: REST versus GraphQL API design
text: REST exposes fixed resource endpoints returning predetermined payloads, while GraphQL lets clients request exactly the fields they need through a single flexible query endpoint.

title: Inverted indexes for full-text search
text: An inverted index maps each term to the list of documents containing it, letting a search engine quickly find candidate documents for a query instead of scanning every document.

title: Bayesian inference networks in information retrieval
text: Inference network retrieval models represent documents, concepts and queries as nodes in a belief network, combining evidence through conditional probabilities to rank documents by their probability of satisfying a query.

title: CLIP: connecting text and images
text: CLIP trains a text encoder and an image encoder jointly so that matching text-image pairs land close together in a shared embedding space, enabling zero-shot text-to-image retrieval and classification.
